name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd.
business_summary: Government-owned (53%) oil marketing and refining company: ~38-40 Mtpa refining at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina (with a petrochemical expansion), ~25% share of India's petrol/diesel/LPG retail via ~23,000 outlets, plus lubricants, aviation fuel and stakes in city-gas distributors. Retail fuel prices are effectively administered, so crude spikes compress marketing margins; Q1 FY27 produced a loss (EBITDA Rs-4,055 cr, PAT Rs-1,873 cr) before Q2 recovered (EBITDA Rs8,973 cr, PAT Rs4,863 cr, -21.5% YoY). TTM sales Rs538,088 cr; market cap Rs1.38 lakh cr; dividend yield 5.6%. Plans a Rs1.45 lakh cr Andhra Pradesh (Ramayapatnam) refinery-petchem complex.

exposures.mechanism: With retail petrol/diesel/LPG prices held steady, crude is the main swing: +10% Brent (~+$9.5/bbl at $95) = ~Rs5.6/l product cost. On ~38 bn litres/yr MS+HSD, 30% passed on over 3 months leaves ~Rs4/l = ~Rs15k cr annualised = -57% of TTM EBITDA Rs26,238 cr; EV/MCap ~1.25, persistence 0.25 (govt compensation/price action fades it) => ~-18 gross; partly offset by inventory gains and refining margin (see F_REFINING_MARGIN) => net ~-5.5. Pack empirical -2.16 (t=-4.4) is from a more regulated regime; ICRA: OMCs lost Rs530 cr/day (2026-09-23). Q1 FY27 EBITDA was Rs-4,055 cr when crude spiked.

evidence.note: ET/Moneycontrol: OMCs lose Rs530 cr daily

exposures.mechanism: ~38-40 Mt crude throughput (~290 mn bbl); +$2/bbl GRM = ~$580 mn = ~Rs5,500 cr = +21% EBITDA; x1.25 x0.4 persistence => +10; central 5 given Bina and product-mix limits. Pack empirical is NEGATIVE (-1.61, t=-3.4): the series is a heating-oil proxy, so it co-moves with diesel spikes that hurt frozen-price marketing; structural sign kept positive, conflict flagged.

evidence.note: empirical -1.61 per +$2 GRM proxy, t=-3.4 (sign conflict)
Investing.com: BPCL Q2 beats on EPS as refining stays strong

exposures.mechanism: +1 unit = Rs2/l excise rise. If retail is frozen the OMC absorbs it: Rs2/l x ~38 bn l = ~Rs7,600 cr = -29% EBITDA x1.25 x0.5 => -18 worst case; probability-weighted vs pass-through to consumers and the current bias toward excise cuts => -4. Centre to decide on the Rs75,000 cr OMC compensation ask in 2027 (Moneycontrol 2026-09-07).
BPCL exports are small but a windfall levy on refiners' export margin was used in 2022; +1 imposition => ~-1.5.

Crude is USD-priced against INR retail prices; +3% INR depreciation raises crude cost like Brent +3% (~-1.65 using the Brent weight) with a small offset from USD-linked GRM on exports. Pack -1.09 (t=-0.8).
Interest Rs2.98k cr TTM on large working-capital borrowing; +25bp ~Rs60 cr (0.2% EBITDA); discount-rate effect on a 5.6% dividend-yield PSU dominates.

evidence.note: TTM interest Rs2,980 cr; dividend yield 5.6%

exposures.mechanism: Russian crude discount of ~$3/bbl on roughly a quarter of intake (model knowledge) = ~Rs2,000 cr = +8% EBITDA x1.25 x0.5 => ~+5 for larger access; central 3. BPCL expects Russian purchases to fall in November (2026-10-26) and a US Russia-sanctions law adds risk, though 100% tariffs on India were waived (2026-10-27).

Excess over the Brent channel: supply security for ~50-55% of crude from the Gulf (model knowledge; BPCL secured 55% of October needs by 2026-08-27), freight and insurance premia, replacement of cargoes (WTI cargo bought 2026-11-03). Peace hopes lowered Brent 8% on 2026-11-02.
Fuel demand grows ~0.8x GDP; +1pp lifts marketing volumes ~0.8% and refinery utilisation; ~+0.6.
Stronger EV push erodes long-run petrol demand (>12m mostly); BPCL's transition capex partly hedges.
Crude freight ~$2-3/bbl of landed cost; +25% adds ~$0.6/bbl, ~-0.4 after partial pass-through.

evidence.note: Reuters: oil surges on more tanker attacks
